text:
Alex: heads-up — Support just escalated a customer who hit a bunch of 429s and then billing checks failed; customer says issue started during a marketing promotion spike earlier today.
Maria: ugh, which rate limit? per-key RPM or token bucket exhaustion? :eyes:
Alex: support pasted logs, looks like per-key token bucket drained and requests were forwarded to fallback model which then blew cost limits. Also some auth retries showed 401s from a rotated key.
Sam: can we reproduce in staging? want to validate sane defaults for RPM/TPM and burst params.
Nina: +1. I can run a smokebench but need repro steps and a load pattern (ramp, sustain, short spikes).
Alex: plan: 1) short warmup to populate KV cache 2) 30s high burst to simulate marketing burst 3) sustained 10m steady-state at target RPM 4) observe token refill/drain and 429 surface.
Chris: for tooling I'd suggest vegeta or k6. vegeta is quick for token-bucket style checks. example below.
Sam: paste the command you used previously?
Chris: here — vegeta example (replace X-API-KEY):

```
echo "GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json
" | vegeta attack -rate=1200 -duration=35s | vegeta report
```

Chris: that hits 1200 req/s for 35s; we should also do a ramp test: start 10/s -> 200/s over 60s -> spike to 800/s for 20s -> sustain 60s at 200/s.
Maria: important: set header X-Project-ID to a staging project and run against the staging rate-limiter config, not prod. also add a small client-id header to simulate many distinct keys.
Alex: metrics to watch in Console: ratelimit/429_count per key, ratelimit/bucket_available_tokens, request.latency.p50/p95, billing/estimated_tokens. Also look for auth.error.
Nina: I ran a quick run on lower scale, saw token refill too slow when burst_capacity=500 and refill_rate=10/s. 429s started ~18s into spike.
Sam: interesting — what were your rpm/tpm equivalents?
Nina: that config roughly equals RPM=600 and TPM=36000 (since refill_rate 10/s -> 600/min).
Chris: proposed sane defaults for new customers (initial tier): RPM per-key = 600, TPM global = 30000, burst_capacity = 800 tokens, burst_window = 60s. These are conservative but avoid quick depletion for short promos.
Maria: Those numbers sound ok but we should validate across different payload sizes. Embeddings + long prompts consume more tokens per request — need token-accounting in tests.
Alex: action items: Sam to run full repro with 3 payload types (short gen, long gen, embeddings) and the ramp/spike pattern in staging by EOD. Nina to add a quick feature-flagged override for burst_capacity for a single customer for tomorrow's test. Chris to capture metrics and draft recommended defaults doc. Maria to double-check auth rotation path to ensure 401s don't cascade to repeated retries.
Sam: I'll start the runs in ~30m. will tag results here and attach vegeta reports.
loadtest-bot: scheduled job started: vegeta-run-1718502468-1 (staging)
Alex: also note: add a guard in billing flow to not re-ingest failed billing events after a 429 flood — prevents double-charges panic.
Nina: added a quick Jira ticket: INFRA-4521 to add per-key burst overrides and safe billing backoff.
Chris: when you post results include the raw rate of 429s and the time-to-recover for token bucket (how long until tokens back to >=50%). that helps pick burst_window.
Sam: will do, starting now. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks all — good triage. we'll iterate on defaults after empirical runs. :white_check_mark:
